pages.title: Management, Licensing & Service Contracts
pages.help: The statewide rules define when compensated management requires Illinois licensure and how association funds must be protected. Actual vendors and agreements remain association-instance facts.

sections.title: Statewide management and licensing framework
sections.help: Current-effective Illinois rules for community association management services.

controls.text: Providing community association management services, acting as a community association manager, or holding oneself out as a community association management firm in Illinois requires a current valid Department license unless a statutory exemption applies.

Community association management includes compensated administration of financial, administrative, maintenance, or other association duties, including control or disbursement of association funds, budget preparation, meeting assistance, record maintenance, contract administration or procurement, and coordination of duties called for in the management contract.

The statutory definition of community association manager excludes support staff such as bookkeepers, administrative assistants, secretaries, property inspectors, and customer service representatives.

Illinois exemptions include uncompensated directors or officers providing management services to their association, persons providing management services to an association of 10 units or less, attorneys acting solely incident to legal practice, specified court-appointed fiduciaries, persons acting within another Illinois professional license, and unlicensed owners or support staff who do not perform licensed activity.

A corporation, partnership, limited liability company, or other legal entity providing community association management services must be licensed as a community association management firm and continuously have a licensed designated community association manager supervising and managing the firm.

A licensed community association manager may not perform activities requiring an Illinois real-estate managing-broker, broker, or residential-leasing-agent license unless the person also holds the required current real-estate license and performs those services under that Act.

sections.title: Association-fund and insurance safeguards
sections.help: Statewide safeguards that apply when licensed management has access to or disburses association funds.

controls.text: A designated community association manager or management firm may not have access to and disburse association funds unless the statutory fidelity-or-crime-insurance conditions are satisfied.

A management firm providing services to more than one community association must maintain separate segregated custodial accounts for each association, in the respective association's name, and may not commingle one association's funds with manager, firm, or other-association funds.

The designated manager or management firm must obtain appropriate general-liability and errors-and-omissions insurance as determined by the Department and provide current certificates to the association within 10 days of an association request.

The Condominium Property Act separately establishes fidelity-bond and segregated-account safeguards for community association managers handling funds, including requirements for associations of 6 or more residential units.

controls.label: Association account / segregation reference
controls.help: Reference or description sufficient to identify how association funds are held. Do not place passwords, account credentials, or secret access material here.

sections.title: Active service-contract inventory
sections.help: Section 19 requires current contracts, leases, and agreements to be kept as association records. This inventory records association-specific agreements without claiming every vendor category has a separate statewide professional-license requirement.

controls.text: The association must keep all contracts, leases, and other agreements then in effect to which the association is a party or under which the association or unit owners have obligations or liabilities.

item_controls.label: Contract value / recurring amount
item_controls.help: Use only when a meaningful amount can be represented without distorting the agreement; otherwise leave blank and use notes.
